messages:
Sam (Acme): Hey team — after we moved to fontana-1.2 yesterday our p99 on /v1/chat jumped a lot for long-context sessions (clients hitting ~8k tokens). p50 looks fine but p99 went from ~1.2s to ~11-14s and some requests are timing out. No prompt changes on our side. Can you triage?

Eli (Support): Thanks for reporting, Sam. I'm taking this. Can you share a sample request id or payload that hit the high latency? Any request ids you can paste will speed repro.

Sam (Acme): request_id=acme-req-20260302-4821 sample prompt (redacted): "[system] ...user history ..." long context with emojis and multi-language snippets. Also attaching client logs showing timeout at 10s.

Eli (Support): Noted. @Lina can you pull recent infra metrics for fontana-1.2 pods serving the customer region? ops-monitor-bot, any automated alerts?

ops-monitor-bot: Alert: fontana-1.2 nodepool us-west-2 high p99 latency spike, started 2026-03-02T14:03:21Z. 95th < svc-slo, 99th > svc-slo. KV cache hit ratio down ~28% vs baseline.

Lina (SRE): I'm seeing the same. p99 spike correlates with increased tokenization time and higher CPU on tokenizer-service instances. KV cache miss rate for long sequences up from 8% -> 41%.

John (ML Onboard): I rolled fontana-1.2 with a tokenizer normalization tweak (unicode NFKC + emoji clustering) to match new training text normalization. It passed canary perf checks but maybe long-context combos hit a slow path.

Miguel (Runtime): Interesting — if tokenizer returns different token boundaries we can get more tokens and more KV cache churn. Do we have token counts for the failing requests vs baseline?

Eli (Support): Sam sent one sample: original model (fontana-1.1) token_count=4120 latency=1.3s; fontana-1.2 token_count=4837 latency=13.1s. Same input.

John (ML Onboard): That's a big delta. The new normalization step can break some byte alignment, so we may be producing a lot of subword fragments for emoji+CJK sequences. I'll run a quick tokenizer diff.

Miguel (Runtime): Also seeing repeated small token outputs in logs causing tiny batches and KV cache thrash. Example runtime trace: 
```
[2026-03-02T14:02:58Z] req=acme-req-4821 model=fontana-1.2 tokens_out_seq_len=4837 tokens_emitted=1..4837 step_latencies_ms=[... large tail ...] kv_cache_misses=412
```
Lina (SRE): For mitigation we should immediately: 1) route affected customer traffic back to fontana-1.1 2) enable aggressive prefix caching for their sessions if possible 3) throttle canary rollout. Thoughts?

Eli (Support): Sam — we can route your tenant back to fontana-1.1 now while we fix. Want to do that? Minimal disruption.

Sam (Acme): Yes please do that ASAP. Our SLAs are getting hit.

Lina (SRE): I'll run the tenant reroute. Command: 
```
# reroute tenant to stable
redwoodctl traffic split set --tenant acme --model fontana --variant v1.1 --weight 100
```
deploy-bot: Started traffic split update for tenant=acme to fontana:v1.1.

deploy-bot: Completed traffic split update. New split: fontana:v1.1=100%.

Eli (Support): Sam, can you confirm client-side if latency returns to baseline after the reroute?

Sam (Acme): Confirmed — p99 back down to ~1.4s within a few minutes. Thanks. :relieved:

John (ML Onboard): Investigating tokenizer diffs now. Quick find: the NFKC normalization merged combined emoji sequences into many U+200D joiner sequences mapping to individual subtokens instead of the old cluster; tokenizer fallback to byte-level normalization path triggered for mixed-script tokens. This explains big token count increase and kv-cache miss.

Miguel (Runtime): Two paths forward: A) patch tokenizer to preserve previous clustering heuristics for mixed emoji/CJK sequences (hotfix), B) add a fast pre-token normalization shim that normalizes only whitespace and NUL removal (cheaper), C) keep fontana-1.2 tokenizer but change routing rules to avoid it for high long-context traffic until tokenization is stable.

John (ML Onboard): I'll open a hotfix PR to revert the emoji clustering change and add unit tests for mixed-script examples. Patch should be quick but needs a release and perf verify.

Lina (SRE): Hotfix timeline? We can keep tenant on v1.1; need to prevent further rollouts. Miguel, can you pause the staged rollout?

Miguel (Runtime): Pausing ongoing canaries now. Command: 
```
redwoodctl rollout pause --model fontana --version 1.2
```
deploy-bot: Rollout for fontana:1.2 paused by miguel at 2026-03-02T14:15:10Z.

John (ML Onboard): Hotfix PR: #4327 — revert emoji clustering + add regression testcases. Estimated deploy after CI in ~45 minutes if green.

Eli (Support): I'll set expectation with Sam: reroute done, rollback in-place until hotfix verified, we'll follow up with postmortem.

Sam (Acme): Appreciate quick action. Please ping me when it's in stable and we can test before re-onboarding.

Lina (SRE): After hotfix we should run a quick synthetic test against a corpus of mixed emoji/CJK long sequences (we'll add samples from Sam) and check token counts + kv-cache hit ratio. If good, resume canary at small percent and monitor p99 for 30m.

Miguel (Runtime): Also enabling an automated check in the onboarding pipeline: token_count_delta <= 10% vs baseline for a long-context test; if exceeded, fail/cancel rollout. I'll open GH issue to track.

John (ML Onboard): CI green, deploying tokenizer-patch to canary pool. Deploy command: 
```
deploy-tool deploy --service tokenizer-service --image fontana-tokenizer:patch-1 --env canary
```
deploy-bot: tokenizer-service patch-1 deployed to canary pool.

ops-monitor-bot: Canary telemetry for tokenizer-service patch-1: token_count_delta median ~+2%, p99 latency shows no regression in 15m window. KV cache miss back to baseline ~9%.

Lina (SRE): Miguel, can you bump acme tenant to test patch in canary (20%) before full resume? We'll watch metrics.

Miguel (Runtime): Done. Command: 
```
redwoodctl traffic split set --tenant acme --model fontana --variants v1.1=80,v1.2-patch1=20
```
deploy-bot: traffic split updated for tenant=acme.

Sam (Acme): Seeing a few requests on the patched variant — numbers look good so far. p99 ~1.5s.

John (ML Onboard): Good signal. I'll schedule canary ramp after a 30m stable period. Also adding the mixed-script test into the onboarding suite to block future regressions.

Eli (Support): Action items summary: 
- tenant rerouted back to fontana-1.1 (done)
- canary paused (done)
- tokenizer hotfix deployed to canary and patch tested (in progress/done)
- migration plan: if 30m stable, ramp to 100% with monitoring, else rollback fully to v1.1
- postmortem to include root cause, test coverage gap, and onboarding pipeline gate (owner: Miguel/John/Lina)

Sam (Acme): Thanks all. Please share the postmortem link when ready.

Lina (SRE): I'll create an incident ticket and link the postmortem. For now closing this triage thread; re-open if anything else shows up. :white_check_mark:
